alignments.note: Inflected passive takes its supplied subject and auxiliaries; rule 17 heads on the lexical verb.
Connective, fronted in English under rule 15.
Dative pronoun; the case preposition rides with it under rule 21, headed on the pronoun.
Anarthrous vocative stands bare, the possessive belonging to the genitive pronoun.
Genitive pronoun carries the possessive; no article stands in the phrase.

Substantival article whose modifier is a bare genitive carrying no verb, so under rule 31's verbless-modifier clause it keeps the antecedent pronoun and the supplied relativizer; head on the nominal word under rule 22.
Genitive name of relationship: rule 52 gives it the whole supplied relational expression 'are of the household of' along with the copula, headed on the name and never on the supplied generic noun.
The ASV writes 'that' for the complement clause, so the conjunction is aligned in the ordinary way under rule 43's English-side test.
Expressed finite verb with the expletive subject English requires; head on the verb word.

review_notes: The supplied 'of the household' is folded onto Chloes under rule 52 rather than marked 'added': no Greek token answers to it and the bare genitive is what carries the relation.
The article at s009 keeps 'them that' and the copula goes with the genitive, following rule 31's verbless-modifier reading; giving the whole 'them that are' to the article is the competing reading.
